questions.question: What does the phrase "the year of less" mean at the beginning of the video?
options: A) A year with fewer holidays and less celebration
B) A year focused on consuming less and embracing minimalism
C) A year with less money available to spend
D) A year with fewer social gatherings
questions.explanation: "The year of less" 指 2026 年呈现出的趋势：人们开始追求更少消费、更少刷社交媒体、更专注于真实生活。这是近年来极简主义和数字排毒（digital detox）潮流的体现，与视频反社交媒体的主题一致。

questions.question: What kind of "posts" is the speaker referring to when they say "you've probably seen posts like this"?
options: A) Academic research articles about technology
B) Job recruitment posts on LinkedIn
C) Social media posts about quitting social media or doing a digital detox
D) News articles covering political events
questions.explanation: 结合视频主题（反社交媒体、回归现实生活），这里的"posts like this"指的是鼓励人们退出社交媒体、进行数字排毒的帖子，反映了当时流行的反社交媒体潮流。

questions.question: What concern does the speaker raise about AI in the video?
options: A) AI is too expensive for most people to use
B) AI will take over all jobs within a few years
C) AI may replace human creativity, family recipes, and personal expression
D) AI cannot understand the English language correctly
questions.explanation: 演讲者担心 AI 会取代家庭食谱（family recipes）并使艺术远离个人表达（art drifts away from personal expression），这是对 AI 时代人文价值流失的担忧，与视频倡导回归真实生活的主题一致。

questions.question: According to the speaker, what positive changes occur when people spend less time on their phones?
options: A) They become richer and more famous
B) They become more patient, more present, and more kind
C) They gain more followers on social media
D) They receive more free product samples
questions.explanation: 演讲者明确指出："We're more patient, more present, more kind." 这是放下手机后人们在心理和人际关系上变得更积极的表现。"present" 在这里是"全神贯注、当下"的意思。

questions.question: What does the word "relearning" imply in "we are relearning how to enjoy our offline life"?
options: A) We are learning about offline life for the very first time
B) We once knew how to enjoy offline life but forgot because of digital distractions
C) Offline life is more difficult than online life
D) We are teaching others about offline life
questions.explanation: "Relearning" 意为"重新学习"，暗示这是一种曾经拥有的能力，因为沉迷于数字设备而暂时遗忘，现在需要重新拾起。这反映了现代社会被科技改变后的一种反思。

questions.question: What is "funny" or ironic about the situation described in the video?
options: A) People are spending much more time on social media than ever before
B) People are using social media to influence each other to leave social media
C) People are making lots of money by posting funny content
D) People are getting bored with funny videos
questions.explanation: 原句 "it's kind of funny that we're influencing each other on social media to get off of social media" 揭示了一种反讽：用社交媒体本身来劝人退出社交媒体。这是社交媒体时代的一种自相矛盾的现象。

questions.question: What does "check out what's going on in social media" mean in everyday English?
options: A) Buy trending products advertised online
B) Browse social media to see updates and news from others
C) Create new posts on social media platforms
D) Delete social media accounts entirely
questions.explanation: "Check out" 在这里是口语化的"看看、浏览"，整句意为"看看社交媒体上发生了什么"，是很多人下意识会做的动作（mindless scrolling），也是演讲者希望人们减少的行为之一。

questions.question: What does the speaker admit about their phone use in the sentence "I had been on my phone probably way too long than I needed to be"?
options: A) They never use their phone at all
B) They probably used their phone much longer than was necessary
C) They used their phone for exactly the right amount of time
D) They used their phone for less time than they wanted
questions.explanation: 原句用过去完成进行时（had been on），强调持续时间。"way too long than I needed" 是非正式但常见的口语表达，意为"远超所需时间"。说话者承认自己刷手机时间过长。

questions.question: What does "jumping to the next thing" describe in the video?
options: A) A type of physical exercise or sport
B) The anxious habit of always moving on without being present
C) Watching a sequence of short videos
D) A popular form of modern dance
questions.explanation: "Jumping to the next thing" 在这里比喻现代人总在不断切换注意力、无法停留在当下的焦虑状态。这也是演讲者希望人们通过远离手机来打破的习惯。

questions.question: According to the speaker, what has "gotten so out of control"?
options: A) Traffic congestion in major cities
B) The number of advertisements being served on social media
C) The art of home cooking
D) The unpredictable weather
questions.explanation: 原句提到 "our favorite influencer, we were served an ad... has gotten so out of control"，指出我们不断被推送广告的现象已经失控，这是社交媒体过度商业化的问题之一。

questions.question: What does the expression "kept hitting ignore" mean in the video?
options: A) Physically hitting an ignore button on a machine
B) Continuously dismissing or not responding to notifications and calls
C) Verbally attacking and ignoring someone
D) Forgetting about a personal problem completely
questions.explanation: "Hitting ignore" 是个口语表达，指对来电或通知按"忽略/拒绝"键（尤其在 iPhone 上是按电源键两次）。"kept hitting ignore" 表示说话者一直选择无视手机的提示。

questions.question: What is the main benefit the speaker has experienced from setting "off hours" with no social media?
options: A) Gaining more followers on social media
B) Being more present and engaged with family during those times
C) Getting bored very easily
D) Losing touch with old friends
questions.explanation: 原句 "this has helped so much in just being more present with my family" 表明设置无社交媒体时间后最大的好处是与家人相处时更专注、更投入。这是视频反复强调的"在场（present）"价值。

questions.question: How does the speaker define "off hours"?
options: A) The hours when they are working at their job
B) The hours during which they are not allowed to use social media
C) Only the late-night sleeping hours
D) The weekend hours only
questions.explanation: 原句 "off hours, it's just, it's no social media time" 直接给出了定义："off hours" 就是不允许刷社交媒体的时间段。视频后面还提到具体是从晚上到第二天早上。

questions.question: Besides getting off the phone, what other benefit does the speaker mention from doing the activity?
options: A) Sleeping much longer hours
B) Feeling like they are creating more
C) Earning more money quickly
D) Getting more social media followers
questions.explanation: 原句 "This not only helps me get off of my phone, but I feel like I'm creating more" 指出除了减少手机使用外，还获得了"创造更多"的成就感，强调了兴趣爱好带来的价值。

questions.question: What activity does the speaker suggest for people who only have 5-10 minutes of free time?
options: A) Quickly checking social media feeds
B) Cooking without multitasking, maybe with a long-form YouTube video
C) Taking a long nap
D) Watching short TV commercials
questions.explanation: 原句 "Cooking without multitasking, maybe putting on a long-form YouTube video if you really need something" 建议在零碎时间里专心做饭（不一心多用），这是替代刷手机、培养专注力的好方法。

questions.question: What daily habit does the speaker recommend for building hobbies?
options: A) Quit all hobbies immediately
B) Only do hobbies on weekends and holidays
C) Spend an hour on a hobby every single day
D) Spend an entire day on hobbies once a month
questions.explanation: 原句 "just spend an hour towards a hobby every single day" 建议每天花一小时投入到爱好中，强调的是持续性（consistency），而不是偶尔的大段时间。

questions.question: What strategy does the speaker recommend for reducing mindless phone use?
options: A) Scrolling even more often to get it out of your system
B) Replacing scrolling with more hobbies and different activities
C) Deleting all apps and throwing away the phone
D) Working longer hours to stay busy
questions.explanation: 原句 "once you start replacing scrolling with more hobbies and you start getting into different..." 建议用爱好取代无意识的滑动屏幕。这是一种正面的替代策略，而不是简单禁止。

questions.question: In the phrase "the more addicting it becomes," what is the implied full comparative structure?
options: A) The more you use it, the more addicting it becomes
B) The more time passes, the more addicting it becomes
C) The more phones are produced, the more addicting they become
D) The more people discuss it, the more addicting it becomes
questions.explanation: 这是英语中"the more..., the more..."（越……就越……）的省略句式。完整结构是 "The more you use it, the more addicting it becomes"（用得越多，就越让人上瘾），用于强调反复使用带来的成瘾性。

questions.question: What does the phrasal verb "step away" mean in the video?
options: A) Walk a long distance physically
B) Take a break or distance from something to gain perspective
C) Move to a different city or country
D) Resign from a job
questions.explanation: "Step away" 在这里是"暂时离开/抽身"的意思，指远离手机或社交媒体一段时间以重新审视生活。"Take time to step away" 意为"花时间抽身出来"。

questions.question: What does "brick it" mean in the phrase "Put your phone away, lock it, brick it"?
options: A) Throw the phone against a brick wall
B) Sell the phone for cash immediately
C) Make the phone completely unusable, as if it were a brick
D) Put a heavy protective case on the phone
questions.explanation: "Brick" 作动词是俚语，意为"使设备变成砖头（即无法使用的电子废物）"。整句是一个递进的幽默表达：把手机收起来 → 锁上 → 让它变成砖头，强调彻底远离手机的决心。

questions.question: What specific challenge does the speaker suggest at the end of the video?
options: A) Using social media even more frequently
B) Using a different camera, like a Polaroid or disposable camera, to take photos
C) Deleting all old photos from the phone
D) Buying the latest, most expensive smartphone
questions.explanation: 原句 "I want you to try to use a different camera to take photos. So maybe a Polaroid, maybe go to Walgreens and get like a $5..." 建议尝试用拍立得或一次性相机拍照，远离手机摄像头，培养不同的拍照体验。

questions.question: The speaker mentions small changes that made the biggest difference. What is one small change you have made (or could make) in your daily routine to reduce phone use and be more present? Describe the change and explain why it works for you.
questions.explanation: 本题为开放式口语题，旨在训练学生用英语描述个人习惯改变并说明原因。建议学生用过去时或现在完成时描述自己的改变，并用 "because/since/as" 等连词解释原因。
questions.referenceAnswer: Sample answer: I started putting my phone in another room before going to bed. I used to scroll for an hour before sleeping, but now I read a book instead. This helps because I'm not tempted to check notifications, and I fall asleep faster. Another change I made was deleting the social media app from my phone for one month. It worked because I had to go to the website on my computer to check it, which made me think twice before opening it.
questions.hint: Think about a specific habit (e.g., putting your phone in another room, deleting one app, setting a no-phone meal time). Describe what you do and why it helps you.

questions.question: The speaker talks about finding hobbies and cooking without getting distracted. What is one hobby or offline activity you genuinely enjoy that doesn't involve a screen? Describe the experience in detail.
questions.explanation: 本题为开放式口语题，鼓励学生分享真实爱好并描述体验细节。可以用感官动词（see, hear, smell, taste, feel）和现在时态来描述活动过程。
questions.referenceAnswer: Sample answer: I really enjoy baking sourdough bread on weekends. I love the feeling of kneading the dough with my hands and watching it slowly rise. The kitchen smells amazing when the bread is baking in the oven, and the taste is so much better than store-bought bread. It also helps me slow down because I have to wait for the dough to proof. I feel really proud when I take the bread out of the oven and share it with my family.
questions.hint: Think of something you can do with your hands or in real life (cooking, reading, knitting, painting, hiking, playing music, etc.). Use sensory details to describe it.

questions.question: The speaker recommends spending an hour a day on a hobby. If you could spend one extra hour every day on a new hobby, what would you choose to learn and why?
questions.explanation: 本题为开放式口语题，考察学生用英语表达愿望和原因。可使用 "I would like to... because..." 或 "If I had an extra hour, I would..." 等句型，并给出至少两个具体理由。
questions.referenceAnswer: Sample answer: If I had an extra hour every day, I would learn to play the ukulele. I have always loved the sound of it, and I think it's a relatively easy instrument to start with. I would choose this hobby because music helps me relax after a long day at work, and I could eventually play songs for my friends. Plus, learning an instrument keeps my mind sharp and gives me a sense of accomplishment when I finally master a new song.
questions.hint: Pick a hobby you have always wanted to try. Explain the reason (relaxation, creativity, skill-building, sharing with others) and what you hope to achieve.

questions.question: The speaker invites viewers to try a digital detox challenge. Pick one specific challenge from the video (or invent your own) that you would like to try, and describe how you think the experience would go for you.
questions.explanation: 本题为开放式口语题，考察学生选择具体挑战并预测自身反应的能力。可使用 "I think I would..." 或 "I would probably feel..." 表达预期，并描述可能遇到的困难和收获。
questions.referenceAnswer: Sample answer: I would like to try the Polaroid camera challenge for one week. I would use a disposable camera instead of my phone to take all my photos. I think the first day would be hard because I am so used to taking dozens of photos with my phone. By the end of the week, I think I would feel more present in the moment because I would only have 27 shots to use, so I would think more carefully about each photo. I would also be more patient and appreciate the anticipation of waiting for the film to be developed.
questions.hint: Choose one challenge (e.g., no phone for 24 hours, using a film camera, no social media after 5pm). Predict how you would feel and what you would learn.
